articles.summary: Presidente americano pediu que Dana White reúna pessoas do mundo das lutas para trabalhar na equipe de comunicação.
articles.body:
Trump convida presidente do UFC para o cargo de porta-voz da Casa Branca — Foto: Jornal Nacional

O presidente Donald Trump escolheu um nome inesperado para assumir o comando da secretaria de comunicação da Casa Branca.

Ele chamou o atual presidente do UFC, a maior organização de artes marciais mistas do mundo, para o cargo de porta-voz.

Trump pediu que Dana White leve pessoas do mundo das lutas para trabalhar como assistentes na equipe de comunicação .

O pedido ocorre na mesma semana em que o governo Trump sofreu uma derrota histórica nas eleições para o novo Congresso americano.

articles.title: Ilia Topuria: "Si me dice que me voy a quedar ciego, que le den a Justin y a todo el mundo"
articles.standfirst: 'El Matador' se sinceró acerca de las lesiones que sufrió en la Casa Blanca ante Gaethje y cómo lo vivió desde dentro
articles.summary: 'El Matador' se sinceró acerca de las lesiones que sufrió en la Casa Blanca ante Gaethje y cómo lo vivió desde dentro
articles.body: El pasado 14 de junio, Ilia Topuria vivió la noche más oscura de su carrera en las MMA tras ser finalizado por Justin Gaethje y perder el invicto y el cinturón de peso ligero. Su hermano Aleksandre decidió parar el combate antes de que diese inicio el quinto asalto, al ver cómo su hermano mayor tenía fracturados los dos orbitales, la nariz y el pie, e Ilia ha hablado al respecto de ese suceso y de cómo lo vivió desde dentro. Antes de que diese comienzo el cuarto asalto, el árbitro Marc Goddard y el doctor ya le dijeron a Ilia que iban a parar el combate al ver cómo tenía el rostro. Sin embargo, 'El Matador' insistió en que estaba bien y logró convencerles por el contexto de la situación. Campeón invicto, en la Casa Blanca, en la cartelera más importante de la historia... No podía acabar así. "Cuando entra el doctor, me dice que me va a parar la pelea y yo le dije que no, que me secara el ojo, que me quitara la sangre, que hiciera algo para que siguiera porque físicamente estaba bien, yo no quería parar. Es una pelea que marca una vida, o varias, no solo la mía y la de Justin", ha revelado en una entrevista con 'ABC'. Sin embargo, cuando su hermano Aleksandre se dió cuenta de la gravedad de la situación y de que era imposible que Ilia diese la vuelta a la pelea en el quinto, decidió que ya era suficiente. Una decisión que salvó la carrera de Topuria, ya que a posteriori se supo que si hubiese seguido recibiendo golpes podría haberse quedado ciego. Demoledor. De hecho, Topuria ha agradecido a su hermano esta decisión de parar la pelea por el hecho de que él nunca hubiese dado el paso. Un peleador no piensa en rendirse cuando está en el octágono, y menos Ilia. Eso sí, si hubiese sabido lo peligroso que era seguir combatiendo ha dejado claro que no habría dudado en rendirse, tal y como ha confirmado una vez ha sabido el riesgo que tomó. "Con que me dijera que no me iba a quedar ciego me valía para seguir. Porque si me dice que me voy a quedar ciego, que le den a Justin y a todo el mundo, porque no quiero nada en mi vida si me voy a quedar ciego", finalizó. Ilia define su lesión en los orbitales como si le hubiesen tirado cristales, ya que le ardían ambos ojos y se le pegaban los párpados por la sangre. Incluso en el segundo asalto ha revelado que no podía ver bien, de ahí que se lanzase a por Gaethje al suelo una vez le dañó con un golpe al hígado. Casi cinco meses después de aquel día, Topuria es consciente de que su carrera pudo haberse acabado, pero ha recibido una segunda oportunidad para redimirse de aquello y demostrar que sigue destinado a convertirse en uno de los mejores de todos los tiempos.

articles.summary: Former WBO cruiserweight champion Chris Billam-Smith gets a long-awaited shot at revenge in London on Saturday. He takes on Cheavon Clarke, the man who beat him in the final of the national championships to set up a place on the British Olympic team 10 years ago.
articles.body:
Eight Rounds Down, Two to Go: Bentley vs. Mosley Jr.

Bentley showed more intent in the seventh, landing a couple of nice rights to take the round.

It's impressive how relentless Mosley Jr.'s pressing still is in the eighth, even after he suffered the early knockdown. He clearly realises there's an opportunity to upset things here, although he will likely need a finish at this point.

articles.title: Denzel Bentley bowls over Shane Mosley Jr but holds on for close but unanimous decision victory at the Copper Box
articles.summary: Denzel Bentley drops Shane Mosley Jr but is pressed in a close fight while American heavyweight hope Da'Mazion Vanhouter dazzles with another first round knockout; Watch Chris Billam-Smith vs Cheavon Clarke live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Bentley, who'd seen the WBO strip him of their middleweight championship in the build up to this fight, looked to take out his frustration on a world-rated opponent .

For a moment, in the early going, it looked like Bentley was going to make swift, brutal work of his opponent, the son of Hall of Famer Shane Mosley.

Mosley would have been happy with the opening round. He took the centre of the ring and used his long left to marshal Bentley. Pressed into a corner and backed up, Bentley threw potshots.

But in the second round Bentley hit with electric intent. A solid right cross shook Mosley up badly and the following cross to the chin sent the American down into the canvas.

Mosley managed to rise and Bentley set about him. But he couldn't land quite cleanly enough to put Mosley down or out and the American got through the round.

By the fifth round Mosley had regrouped as he worked on the front foot. His right pinged Bentley and he attacked the Londoner on the ropes.

Bentley was too static as dynamism drained from his work. It invited the American to come forward and work. Mosley finished the seventh round letting his hands go as Bentley spun away.

The Londoner fired off bursts of punches and a cut by Mosley's right eye did worsen. Single shots in the closing stages clipped Mosley, but Bentley didn't shake him up as he had earlier on.

It left Bentley with a nervy wait for the scorecards but he came through on a unanimous but close decision, 96-94, 96-93 and 95-94.

American heavyweight hope Da'Mazion Vanhouter was too powerful and had too much sheer speed for Ivan Balaz.

Balaz began jabbing, but his left was sluggish and Vanhouter smiled. He powered punches into the Czech's long body and then, with an audible crack, a left hook to the ribs dropped Balaz to his knee with a wince.

Vanhouter celebrated but Balaz just beat the count - only for huge shots to scrape across and plunge him back to the canvas.

Bravely Balaz rose, but Vanhouter ripped his right hook into the body and put him down a third time to end the fight. That was the 10th first-round knockout in the 21-year-old's 14-bout pro career.

Lucas Roehrig displayed fine finishing instincts to stop Connal McDonald in the seventh of eight scheduled rounds.

Roehrig's advantage in speed was clear in the opening round, when he lashed in a lead left hook flush.

He found openings for his rapid right cross but McDonald proved tough and could take his power early on.

The Scotsman pushed himself forward to apply pressure, chopping his left hook and jolting Roehrig with a right.

But the Londoner sucked in air and took his work up a gear in the sixth round, moving and jabbing well.

When he had McDonald hurt in the seventh he didn't let up, striking in shuddering head shots to hack McDonald off his feet and end it.

Sam Hickey patiently fielded the attacks of Amaury Massenaux, blocking the Belgian's hooks with tight elbows. He tested out his uppercut and would use that shot as a weapon to hurt Massenaux.

Hickey had looked to counter, but upped the pressure on Massenaux in the fourth round. A one-two arrowed in and the Scotsman began to crank in powershots.

He applied more of the same in the fifth round. His right hook landed round the side of the head and a right uppercut-left hook combination fired home at close range.

Massenaux backpedalled and dropped to a knee. On resumption Hickey hunted him down and when the referee saw the Belgian hurt, he stepped in to end it.

From the opening bell Kayla Allen waded into Julia Igel, clattering her onto the backfoot with unwavering aggression.

Igel covered up, blocked plenty of punches and threw back, but the assault from Allen kept on coming. Right hands from Allen poured in and she drove left hooks into the body.

Her pace only began to dwindle in the last round and Igel swung wildly as she briefly found herself on the front foot.

But she couldn't break through and Allen won 58-56 after six rounds.

Austrian southpaw Umar Dzambekov continued his unbeaten run with a tremendous one-punch finish to take out world-class contender Zach Parker.

The two were evenly matched, boxing with precision over the opening three rounds of their scheduled 10-rounder, Parker cleverly targeting Dzambekov's body with solid right hooks.

But in the fourth round, Dzambekov drilled him with a thudding left uppercut to the solar plexus. Parker folded over the punch, crumpled to the canvas and just could not beat the referee's count.

Masood Abdulah opened the show winning an excellent eight-rounder against American prospect Adan Palma.

A flashing left from Abdulah streaked across in the first round to drop the visitor on the seat of his shorts.

But Palma struck back in the fourth round. He popped Abdulah with a hard left hook and the Londoner's legs wobbled beneath him. Abdulah kept himself upright but he was hard-pressed.

In the fifth round Palma shook Abdulah up with a right but in the sixth round the home fighter managed to reassert control, dropping the American with another well-timed left hook.

Abdulah took a unanimous decision, 78-72, 77-73 and 76-74 on the cards.

Vinnie Kemp , nicknamed the "King of Violence," made an impression. He swaggered into the ring, was reprimanded for barracking Liam McElhinney and battered his opponent into the ropes with wide-armed punches, ending it inside the first round.

articles.title: 'Please take the job!' - Trump asks UFC boss Dana White to be White House press secretary
articles.summary: The BBC has asked the White House and UFC whether the president's job offer is genuine.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump has asked Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss Dana White to be White House press secretary, in a social media post.

"Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Dana, please take the job!"

It's unclear whether the president's public job offer is genuine. The BBC has asked the White House and UFC, along with its parent company TKO Group Holdings, for comment.

The vacancy for White House press secretary has been open since mid-October, when Katie Zacharia exited after just a few days on the job.

Trump's post comes after his fellow Republicans were routed in the US midterm elections, losing their congressional majorities.

In Saturday afternoon's post, Trump called White "a violent Fighter and Warrior" and asked that he bring a number of high-profile UFC fighters with him on the job "even though some are not from our Country".

"We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left," Trump wrote, alongside photos of the six fighters.

Following Trump's post, White posted an Instagram photo of himself behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room.

"On to the next chapter," White's post said, though it was unclear if the post was tongue-in-cheek.

White, who is also the chief of Zuffa Boxing, was ringside for a fight in London on Saturday between British former world champion Chris Billam-Smith and Jamaican-born Briton Cheavon Clarke at the Copper Box Arena.

The BBC was trying to reach him for comment.

Famously combative, White has at times clashed with journalists covering the sport during news conferences.

In 2020, he released a video targeting reporters who had questioned the UFC's decision to hold fights early in the pandemic.

In 2009, he released an expletive-laden video tirade using an anti-gay slur while rebutting a journalist's story about changes to backstage credentialing rules at UFC events.

White is a longtime ally - and friend - of Trump.

When White and his business partners bought the then-struggling UFC organisation for $2m in 2001, the sport was facing intense bipartisan backlash.

Just five years earlier, Republican Senator John McCain had famously labelled mixed martial arts "human cockfighting", sparking bans in 36 US states.

"None of the venues wanted [the UFC]," White told CBS, the BBC's US partner, in 2025. "They didn't believe in it. They didn't like it, and they were worried about the type of crowd that would show up for this type of event."

With mainstream arenas shutting them out, White credits Trump with saving the organisation by hosting two UFC events at the Trump Taj Mahal casino in Atlantic City, New Jersey, in 2001.

This summer, the UFC held a cage match on the White House lawn.

White became a speaker for Trump's White House campaigns at the Republican National Conventions in 2016, 2020 and 2024.

articles.title: Donald Trump ofrece a Dana White, presidente de la UFC, ser el nuevo secretario de prensa de la Casa Blanca
articles.standfirst: Ambos guardan una gran relación desde hace años
articles.summary: Ambos guardan una gran relación desde hace años
articles.body: Ver para creer. Según ha comunicado el propio Donald Trump, el presidente estadounidense ha pedido al presidente de la UFC, Dana White, que sea el nuevo secretario de prensa de la Casa Blanca. Ambos, cabe recordar, guardan una gran relación desde hace años, se les ha visto hacer campaña (a favor de Trump) juntos e incluso Dana White 'entregó' a Trump el pasado UFC Casa Blanca de junio (en el que Topuria perdió ante Gaethje) como regalo de cumpleaños al mandatario. "Dana será un secretario de prensa como ningún otro", escribió Trump en su plataforma 'Truth Social'. "¡Dana, por favor, acepta el puesto!", ampliaba. Este aún no se ha pronunciado. Pero no acaba ahí. Trump ha pedido a Dana White, definido por el presidente de los Estados Unidos como "un violento luchador y guerrero", que incorpore a su equipo a varios peleadores o ex peleadores de la UFC. "He solicitado que traiga consigo a un equipo de colaboradores, algunos de los cuales no son de nuestro país, entre ellos Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes y Kayla Harrison", escribía Trump.

articles.title: Trump Says He's Asked UFC's Dana White to Be His Press Secretary. No One Will Say If He's Joking
articles.summary: WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White, an announcement unconventional even for the norm-busting president and one that nobody in the White House immediately confirmed.
articles.body:
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White, an announcement unconventional even for the norm-busting president and one that nobody in the White House immediately confirmed.

Trump, while he was at his golf club in Florida, posted on social media that he made the offer to "the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior" to become the Republican president's chief spokesperson.

Trump said he requested that White bring along several UFC fighters as "assistants," adding, "We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!"

The White House did not respond Saturday to messages inquiring about the Truth Social post.

White was in London on Saturday for a boxing event. A spokesperson for UFC did not immediately respond to messages seeking comment.

The UFC head shared an image of Trump's post on Instagram, along with an image of himself standing behind the podium in the White House press briefing room with the words "On to the next chapter."

Trump's post came as his White House is in a period of major transition and struggling with his party's deep losses in Tuesday's midterm elections. The historic wins by Democratic candidates, including in areas that Republicans had held for decades, led to the GOP losing control of both chambers of Congress.

Trump on Friday announced he was replacing his longtime adviser Susie Wiles, who was seen as something of a tempering force on the president's impulses, with aide Stephen Miller to serve as the next chief of staff. Miller is known as the architect of the administration's hard-line immigration policies and is among the most determined of Trump's inner circle.

The shake-up at the heart of his administration follows the brief but tumultuous week when Trump tried out a new press secretary in Katie Zacharia, who seemed uncomfortable in her sole appearance before reporters before leaving the job after five days.

The post had been vacant since Karoline Leavitt left at the end of August. Trump remains without a chief spokesperson.

Trump is close friends with White and has attended several UFC events with him since returning to the White House in January 2025.

He brought White and the sport to the White House's South Lawn in June for the celebration of America's 250th year of its independence and the president's own 80th birthday. A wire-mesh Octagon was constructed near the executive mansion under " The Claw," a spaceship-like metal arch fitted with lights, sound equipment and large screens.

"It was an amazing experience, this was a one-of-one," said White afterward.

White also spoke at the Republican National Conventions in 2016, 2020 and 2024.

articles.title: UFC's Dana White Says He Will Meet With Trump Monday Over Offer to be White House Press Secretary
articles.summary: WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White, an announcement unconventional even for the norm-busting president. White said Saturday that he plans to meet with Trump on Monday at the White House.
articles.body:
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White, an announcement unconventional even for the norm-busting president. White said Saturday that he plans to meet with Trump on Monday at the White House.

Trump, while he was at his golf club in Florida, posted on social media that he made the offer to "the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior" to become the Republican president's chief spokesperson.

White, who was in London on Saturday for a boxing event, was asked at a news conference about Trump's post and responded by saying that he planned to fly to Washington right after and meet with Trump on Monday.

When asked how he would balance the job with the current positions he has in the fighting world, White seemed confused by the question and then said, "Yeah, I got a lot of jobs already."

He declined to say what conversations he'd had with Trump but said, "I'm sure I'll have more to talk about after that."

Before the news conference, the UFC head shared an image of Trump's post on Instagram, along with an image of himself standing behind the podium in the White House press briefing room with the words "On to the next chapter."

The White House and a spokesperson for the UFC did not respond Saturday to messages inquiring about the Truth Social post.

Trump said in his post that he requested that White bring along several UFC fighters as "assistants," adding, "We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!"

While White didn't make it clear if he was seriously considering the position of becoming the primary spokesperson for the president of the United States, he did elsewhere in his news conference describe his ambitions to expand the Zuffa Boxing organization he also runs with Saudi Arabian backers and hold more of its events around the world.

Trump's post came as his White House is in a period of major transition and struggling with his party's deep losses in Tuesday's midterm elections. The historic wins by Democratic candidates, including in areas that Republicans had held for decades, led to the GOP losing control of both chambers of Congress.

Trump on Friday announced he was replacing his longtime adviser Susie Wiles, who was seen as something of a tempering force on the president's impulses, with aide Stephen Miller to serve as the next chief of staff. Miller is known as the architect of the administration's hard-line immigration policies and is among the most determined of Trump's inner circle.

The shake-up at the heart of his administration follows the brief but tumultuous week when Trump tried out a new press secretary in Katie Zacharia, who seemed uncomfortable in her sole appearance before reporters before leaving the job after five days.

The post had been vacant since Karoline Leavitt left at the end of August. Trump remains without a chief spokesperson.

Trump is close friends with White and has attended several UFC events with him since returning to the White House in January 2025.

He brought White and the sport to the White House's South Lawn in June for the celebration of America's 250th year of its independence and the president's own 80th birthday. A wire-mesh Octagon was constructed near the executive mansion under " The Claw," a spaceship-like metal arch fitted with lights, sound equipment and large screens.

"It was an amazing experience, this was a one-of-one," said White afterward.

White also spoke at the Republican National Conventions in 2016, 2020 and 2024.

articles.title: Donald Trump offers White House press secretary job to UFC CEO Dana White
articles.summary: Trump announced his offer to White on his Truth Social platform, referring to the UFC chief as "a violent warrior."
articles.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump offered the open White House press secretary position to UFC chief executive Dana White in a social media post on Saturday.

"I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," Trump wrote in a post on his Truth Social platform. "I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris," Trump added. "We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job! President DONALD J. TRUMP"

"I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," Trump wrote in a post on his Truth Social platform.

"I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris," Trump added. "We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job! President DONALD J. TRUMP"

Trump name-dropped several UFC fighters that White could presumably bring with him to the White House podium to interact with reporters. However, he mistyped the name of Kayla Harrison, arguably the top women's fighter in the world . A two-time Olympic gold medalist and UFC bantamweight champion, Harrison will defend her title at next week's UFC 334 event at New York's Madison Square Garden.

The White House has not officially responded to Trump's post, creating some uncertainty as to whether or not this was a serious invitation, according to the Associated Pres s .

White, in London for Saturday's Zuffa Boxing 12 event , also has not directly responded to the president's announcement. However, he posted a screen shot of Trump's announcement on an Instagram story, along with an image of himself at the podium of the White House press briefing room with the caption, "On to the next chapter."

Trump and White have known each other for at least 25 years

The relationship between the U.S. president and White dates back to 2001, when Trump's Taj Mahal hotel and casino in Atlantic City, New Jersey hosted a UFC event. At the time, New Jersey was one of the few states that sanctioned UFC cards, which were banned in 36 states.

Since then, the two have developed a friendship as Trump has attended several UFC events over the past 25 years — including four as sitting U.S. president. White introduced Trump at the 2024 Republican National Convention, in addition to speaking at the 2016 and 2020 events.

The most public display of the Trump-White partnership was the UFC Freedom 250 event that was held on the South Lawn of the White House in June. The main event of that card was an upset win by UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje , whose name was referenced in Trump's Truth Social post.

UFC holding an event at the White House raised White's already high profile , resulting in interviews with NPR, Rolling Stone and the New Yorker, and an appearance on the cover of Time magazine. White defended Trump in those interviews and implied that he had an advisory role during the 2024 presidential campaign.

The press secretary position became open just over two weeks ago when Katie Zacharia resigned after only five days on the job . Previously a conservative commentator and advisor for the company that runs Truth Social, Zacharia received immediate scrutiny after an initial press briefing that lasted only five minutes, followed by questions over whether she was actually a lawyer , as claimed.

Zacharia took over for Karoline Leavitt, who left the press secretary role in August following the birth of her second child. During Leavitt's maternity leave, other officials in the Trump administration held press briefings, including Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

articles.title: Cheavon Clarke hands Chris Billam-Smith first stoppage loss in stunning upset win over former world champion
articles.summary: Cheavon Clarke beat former world champion Chris Billam-Smith at the Copper Box Arena in London; Billam-Smith had never been dropped before but Clarke put him over twice before the referee halted the Bournemouth star
articles.body:
He not only knocked the former world champion down for the first time in Billam-Smith's career, he put him over twice and handed the Bournemouth star a first stoppage defeat.

Halted on the ropes, as Clarke's right hooks streaked in, Billam-Smith at once shook his head to protest as the referee waved it off.

Clarke, after a thrilling win over Jack Massey last time out, was looking for a big-name scalp that would launch him into the top class of the division. He got it.

Billam-Smith had been seeking to exact some personal vengeance too. Clarke had beaten him in a pivotal national amateur championship final 10 years ago. The Bournemouth man had subsequently converted himself from amateur nearly man to elite professional champion. But, a decade on, Clarke once again handed him a bitterly painful defeat.

They began the first round busily with frenetic work. Clarke, full of energy, winged shots over. His head swung in too wildly, but it was a right hand over the top that gave Billam-Smith pause for thought.

Clarke popped Billam-Smith with a left hook as the former champion charged after him. Rolling under a left hook, Clarke moved off. He snuck his right round Billam-Smith's guard. Billam-Smith swallowed another right but dug in an uppercut with his backhand.

A right flew in and Clarke grabbed him in a clinch. He then answered with a crack right to the jaw himself. But Billam-Smith, renowned for his toughness, took it stolidly.

In the third round Clarke blasted an excellent right uppercut between Billam-Smith's elbows. He touched his chin with the left hook and reached Billam-Smith with a long cross.

Manoeuvring for position in a clinch, Clarke whipped his left hook over. Billam-Smith bulled into him in a physical, frenetic fight, finishing the fourth round swinging hooks.

Early in the fifth round Clarke went for Billam-Smith. They traded hard hits.

The clinching, a frequent feature of the fight, appeared to leave them both frustrated. Clarke popped in a clean jab, but Billam-Smith ground forward onto the front foot.

Billam-Smith hit out with thudding power in the sixth round. Clarke sighed out a breath and stepped back, briefly losing the shape of his boxing.

But in the seventh round it was stunning to see Clarke bomb Billam-Smith over with a right. The Bournemouth man struggled back to his feet and Clarke swarmed forward. As Billam-Smith tried to escape from the ropes, Clarke knocked him down again.

He attacked Billam-Smith once more on the ropes. Billam-Smith's leg stuttered, but he had his feet under him when referee Lee Every moved in to end it.

"I'm fine. It was a good shot. He buzzed me, obviously," Billam-Smith said afterwards. "It was a great shot. I made a mistake, but I felt like I was winning the fight.

"Fair play to Chev. We've had three fights now and he's got them all. I'd love to run it back and get him eventually."

Clarke beamed: "Underdog to who? Not us!

"I don't care about a label. I'm Chev Clarke and that's all that matters."

Image: Cheavon Clarke was coming off a thrilling victory over Jack Massey in last fight

articles.title: Willy Hutchinson crowned as new  WBC light-heavyweight champion after beating Joshua Buatsi in rematch
articles.summary: Willy Hutchinson defeats Joshua Buatsi by unanimous decision to become the new WBC light-heavyweight champion with scores of 115-113, 115-113 and 117-112 in Manchester; the Scotsman had lost to Buatsi by split decision in their first fight in 2024; Buatsi suffers second loss of pro career
articles.body:
The Scotsman lost to Buatsi by split decision in their first fight in 2024, but Hutchinson won their rematch by unanimous decision with scores of 115-113, 115-113 and 117-112 in Manchester.

Hutchinson took a firm grip on the fight in the early rounds as he frustrated Buatsi with his swift hand speed and elusive movement.

Buatsi had floored Hutchinson twice in their previous fight, but he struggled to land hurtful shots on his fleet-footed rival, who was countering with quick combinations.

In the second half of the fight, Buatsi showed more urgency, closing the range on Hutchinson and lashing in punches from head to body.

But Hutchinson remained on the back foot in the final round, content with his lead on the scorecards, and closed out a sweet victory to secure the vacant WBC belt.

Anthony Yarde, who was watching from ringside, might have been denied a long-awaited fight against British rival Buatsi, but could now switch his sights to a fight against Hutchinson.

Buatsi suffered the second loss of his professional career following a points loss to Callum Smith in another domestic clash in 2025.

images.caption: Image: Willy Hutchinson defeated Joshua Buatsi on points in Manchester
Image: Hutchinson closed out a unanimous decision victory over Buatsi

articles.title: Buatsi vs Hutchinson 2: Scotland's Willy Hutchinson wins WBC light-heavyweight title
articles.summary: Willy Hutchinson is crowned WBC light-heavyweight champion as he produces the performance of his career against Joshua Buatsi in Manchester.
articles.body:
Willy Hutchinson was crowned the WBC light-heavyweight champion after he produced the performance of his career to beat Joshua Buatsi in Manchester.

Hutchinson, 28, edged the tense rematch with the judges scoring it 117-112, 115-113, 115-113 to avenge his defeat by Buatsi in 2024.

Saturday's contest was initially for the interim title but was upgraded when American David Benavidez gave up the WBC gold to move up to cruiserweight.

It was a childhood dream come true for Scotland's Hutchinson, who said before the fight he wrote about his dreams of becoming a WBC champion at the age of 13.

An emotional Hutchinson said after his win was confirmed: "I want to tell the story one more time. I was 13-years-old. My dad was working in Sweden. I signed it in a book, I said I will become a world champion. Let's go!

"Can I say thank you to my coach because I'll you one thing, without him I don't think I'll be here today let alone boxing. This man dug me out of a hole that I never thought that I would get out of, so this is all a bonus baby."

Ticket sales were modest for a world title fight as it was clear that it did not capture the attention of the British public. But those inside made the atmosphere as raucous as possible, with the Manchester crowd favouring Hutchinson.

And they were delighted when the result was read out and Hutchinson became the eighth British light-heavyweight champion - the first since Nathan Cleverly in 2017.

Hutchinson improved his record to 21 victories with two defeats, while it is the second time Londoner Buatsi has lost in 22 professional fights.

Hutchinson shows class to join British elite

Fight week was dominated by predictions that Buatsi, five years Hutchinson's senior, is over the hill.

And the Londoner did nothing to prove otherwise as Hutchinson often toyed with his opponent in the centre of the ring.

The first fight in 2024 had Buatsi walking to the ring as a comfortable favourite, and he backed that up with crushing body shots to send Hutchinson tumbling twice.

But this time around, Hutchinson was a different fighter. In his own words, he had "matured" after picking up two wins since last facing Buatsi.

Hutchinson clearly had the crowd on his side as he made the walk to cheers, while Buatsi was met by a chorus of boos as he paraded around the ring before the bell.

For Buatsi, the strategy was very much the same as the first encounter - whip shots into the body - but Hutchinson now had answers.

The AO Arena is famous for its boxing nights with the city's favourite boxing son, Ricky Hatton, becoming world champion here for the first time in June 2005 in a thriller against Kostya Tszyu.

This did not reach those heights, as the upper tier was closed off because of a lack of ticket sales - and fans of Manchester's Jack Rafferty departed after he won the co-main event.

This did not deter Hutchinson from advancing in the latter rounds and landing rapid triple jabs, while also switching stances.

As Manchester royalty Bez, of the Happy Mondays, watched on from ringside, Hutchinson's corner told him "three rounds and you're a world champion" after the ninth.

And they were right. Despite Buatsi's advances late on, Hutchinson held out to become world champion for the first time.

Being world champion means Hutchinson will be a wanted man in the light-heavyweight division.

Former world title challenger Anthony Yarde was perched ringside and that is a fight that could thrill British boxing fans - now with gold involved, could it happen?

Hutchinson addressed Yarde, who stepped into the ring and said "he's no walkover but let's go. Him next."

But if Hutchinson v Yarde does not come to fruition, then there is the small matter of Dmitry Bivol v Callum Smith for the other three light-heavyweight titles on 12 December.

Whoever wins that could be Hutchinson's next opponent in what would be a huge undisputed bout in 2027.

Domestic rival in Ben Whittaker, who is ranked third with the WBC and holds the silver title, could also emerge as a potential option.

Image caption, Willy Hutchinson made his professional debut in 2017

articles.title: Dana White 'flying to Washington' after Donald Trump offers UFC boss White House press secretary job
articles.summary: White is set to meet with U.S. President Trump on Monday in the nation's capital.
articles.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump offered the open White House press secretary position to UFC chief executive Dana White in a social media post on Saturday.

"I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," Trump wrote in a post on his Truth Social platform. "I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris," Trump added. "We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job! President DONALD J. TRUMP"

"I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," Trump wrote in a post on his Truth Social platform.

"I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris," Trump added. "We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job! President DONALD J. TRUMP"

Trump name-dropped several UFC fighters that White could presumably bring with him to the White House podium to interact with reporters. However, he mistyped the name of Kayla Harrison, arguably the top women's fighter in the world . A two-time Olympic gold medalist and UFC bantamweight champion, Harrison will defend her title at next week's UFC 334 event at New York's Madison Square Garden.

The White House has not officially responded to Trump's post, creating some uncertainty as to whether or not this was a serious invitation, according to the Associated Pres s .

White, in London for Saturday's Zuffa Boxing 12 event , initially posted a screen shot of Trump's announcement on an Instagram story, along with an image of himself at the podium of the White House press briefing room with the caption, "On to the next chapter."

The UFC CEO then gave formal comment on Trump's offer at the event's post-fight media availability, stating that he was "flying to Washington D.C." directly after the news conference in order to meet with the U.S. president.

"I've got a lot of jobs already," White said. "We have a meeting on Monday, so I'm sure I'll have more to talk about after that."

White ultimately declined to further elaborate on whether he's interested in the position.

"I have a meeting on Monday," he reiterated. "I'm flying to D.C. right now, and I'm sure we'll have something to talk about after that."

Prior to White's comments, CNN's Brian Stelter reported that White had declined Trump's offer , though White's latest remarks only invite further questioning of the situation.

There has also been speculation on social media that a different Dana White was actually suggested to Trump, but he thought of the UFC CEO. Dana W. White, who was previously the Assistant to Secretary of Defense for Public Affairs in addition to working for the Heritage Foundation and Fox News, would be a more conventional choice for press secretary. However, that has not been confirmed.

Trump and White have known each other for at least 25 years

The relationship between the U.S. president and White dates back to 2001, when Trump's Taj Mahal hotel and casino in Atlantic City, New Jersey hosted a UFC event. At the time, New Jersey was one of the few states that sanctioned UFC cards, which were banned in 36 states.

Since then, the two have developed a friendship as Trump has attended several UFC events over the past 25 years — including four as sitting U.S. president. White introduced Trump at the 2024 Republican National Convention, in addition to speaking at the 2016 and 2020 events.

The most public display of the Trump-White partnership was the UFC Freedom 250 event that was held on the South Lawn of the White House in June. The main event of that card was an upset win by UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje , whose name was referenced in Trump's Truth Social post.

UFC holding an event at the White House raised White's already high profile , resulting in interviews with NPR, Rolling Stone and the New Yorker, and an appearance on the cover of Time magazine. White defended Trump in those interviews and implied that he had an advisory role during the 2024 presidential campaign.

The press secretary position became open just over two weeks ago when Katie Zacharia resigned after only five days on the job . Previously a conservative commentator and advisor for the company that runs Truth Social, Zacharia received immediate scrutiny after an initial press briefing that lasted only five minutes, followed by questions over whether she was actually a lawyer , as claimed.

Zacharia took over for Karoline Leavitt, who left the press secretary role in August following the birth of her second child. During Leavitt's maternity leave, other officials in the Trump administration held press briefings, including Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

articles.title: Chev Clarke beats Chris Billam-Smith at London's Copper Box arena
articles.summary: Former cruiserweight world champion Chris Billam-Smith is knocked down and stopped for the first time in his professional career as Chev Clarke wins their non-title bout.
articles.body:
Former cruiserweight world champion Chris Billam-Smith was knocked down and stopped for the first time in his career as Chev Clarke won their all-British non-title fight on Saturday.

Londoner Clarke landed a big right hand at the start of the seventh round and although Billam-Smith beat the count, he was down again moments later after a barrage of punches.

The contest was allowed to continue but the Bournemouth fighter looked unsteady on his legs and when Clarke connected with two more blows, the referee stepped in.

Billam-Smith immediately protested against the decision, while Clarke stood in the middle of the ring shrugging his shoulders.

Clarke moves to 13 wins with two defeats and inflicts the third professional defeat for Billam-Smith who also lost to Gilberto Ramirez in 2024 and Richard Riakporhe in 2019.

"I do what champions do," said Clarke, who also beat Billam-Smith when they met in the amateur ranks a decade ago.

"I'm happy. Arsenal won and I won. My training camp was good and you saw that in the ring. I'll take all-comers going forward."

The likes of heavyweight Johnny Fisher, Traitors star King Kenny and strongman Eddie Hall were all spotted watching on from ringside in a Copper Box arena that was far from full, with just the lower tier of seats open for fans.

After a slow start to the contest with lots of holding, Clarke looked the sharper man as he landed some clean shots on the former world champion.

In the second round, the Londoner landed a big overhand right to the side of Billam-Smith's head. Clarke also connected in the third round with a big uppercut and an overhand right that snapped back Billam-Smith's head.

The former world champion, struggling to find his rhythm, was caught by another uppercut before Billam-Smith responded with a short right hook that made Clarke stumble back to his corner.

But in the seventh round Clarke broke Billam-Smith down, scoring two quick knockdowns before the referee intervened.

Fight promoter Dana White said after the fight that he felt the decision to stop the fight might have been a little premature.

Bentley beats bloodied Mosley Jr and calls out Benn

In the main support bout, Britain's Denzel Bentley beat a bloodied and brave Shane Mosley Jr, out-classing the American to win via a unanimous points decision.

Bentley scored a big knockdown in the second round, landing a straight right hand that made Mosley stagger backwards before following up with another right hand that dropped him to the canvas.

Mosley survived the count and the rest of the round but was routinely tagged by Bentley throughout the contest.

The Londonder landed sharp shots off the back foot and in the fifth round drew blood over the right eye of Mosley.

Bentley ended the fight strongly, boxing at times with his hands down and moving round his opponent as he landed eye-catching shots that attracted applause from the fans.

After 10 rounds the scorecards read 96-94 96-93 95-94 in Bentley's favour, with the 31-year-old then pointing at Conor Benn in the audience and suggesting a potential future match-up between the two.

Bentley was stripped of his WBO middleweight title in late October having agreed to fight Mosley instead of face his mandatory challenger.

His interim title was previously elevated to a full world championship belt following Janibek Alimkhanuly's decision to move up to super-middleweight.

Image caption, Denzel Bentley won by unanimous decision in London

articles.title: UFC Vegas 124 live results, highlights, play-by-play
articles.summary: UFC Vegas 124 results, highlights, live discussion and instant play-by-play, reactions and analysis.
articles.body:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is live TONIGHT (Sat., Nov. 7, 2026) with UFC Vegas 124 , streaming live online via Paramount+ . The event goes down inside the familiar META APEX in Las Vegas, Nevada. The main event was supposed to be Sean Brady vs. Gabriel Bonfim ; however, a nasty infection ruined that . Sliding in will be Waldo Cortes-Acosta vs. Johnny Walker in the Heavyweight division.

UFC remains inside Meta APEX for the second straight week here, with Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker as the main event. Cortes-Acosta has found himself off the pace in the title chase lately, after coughing up two decision losses in a row. Walker, meanwhile, introduced himself to the "Land of the Giants" with a cracking knockout over Mick Parkin earlier this year ( re-live that here ).

The co-main event has Tatiana Suarez vs. Virna Jandiroba . Both these women had unsuccessful title challenges in recent years. This bout might determine which among them has any shot of getting a second title fight at 115 pounds.

Rounding out the main card is Davey Grant vs. Elijah Smith , Billy Elekana vs. Lucas Fernando , Priscila Cachoeira vs. Nina Milosevic and Mitch Raposo vs. Marcus Degli . Smith, Fernando, Milosevic and Degli are the showcase fighters here. UFC will be hoping each of those produces a highlight reel finish.

The featured "Prelims" bout is Road to UFC winner, Keiichiro Nakamura , taking on Ollie Schmid . There are some established veterans on the undercard, too, with Andre Petroski meeting Mantas Kondratavicius , Wellington Turman returning to face Seokhyeon Ko and Karine Silva taking on Gabriella Fernandes .

The "Prelims" also include Thomas Petersen vs. Gabriel Lorenco , Jose Delano vs Murtazali Magomedov , Austin Bashi vs. Carlos Calderon and Jonny Parsons vs. Jose Souza .

We are back in the APEX tonight and that means a return to our usual broadcast times.

UFC Vegas 124 "Prelims" will begin at 5 p.m. ET .

UFC Vegas 124 main card is scheduled to start at 8 p.m. ET .

All of UFC Vegas 124 airs on Paramount+ , which you can stream here .

The live blog here starts rolling below at 5 p.m. ET . Come in and say hi!

265 lbs.: Waldo Cortes-Acosta vs. Johnny Walker

115 lbs.: Tatiana Suarez vs. Virna Jandiroba

205 lbs.: Billy Elekana vs. Lucas Fernando

135 lbs.: Priscila Cachoeira vs. Nina Milosevic

145 lbs.: Ollie Schmid def. Keiichiro Nakamura by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)

265 lbs.: Thomas Petersen def. Gabriel Lorenco by TKO (ground and pound), round 3 (4:47)

125 lbs.: Karine Silva def. Gabriella Fernandes by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)

145 lbs.: Murtazali Magomedov def. Jose Delano by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)

145 lbs.: Austin Bashi def. Carlos Calderon by submission (rear naked choke), round 1 (1:07) — HIGHLIGHTS

185 lbs.: Andre Petroski def. Mantas Kondratavicius by TKO (ground and pound), round 2 (4:39)

170 lbs.: Seokhyeon Ko def. Wellington Turman by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)

170 lbs.: Jose Souza def. Jonny Parsons by KO (punches), round 2 (4:16) — HIGHLIGHTS

Keiichiro Nakamura vs. Ollie Schmid: Nakamura and Schmid were very well matched in this fight and we had a decent kickboxing bout between the two. Schmid won many of the exchanges and showed off a particularly impressive kicking game. Nakamaura almost won the fight in the third, knocking down Schmid and then almost pounding him out. That almost gave him his second third round comeback in a row. Schmid gutted it out, though, and earned the decision.

Official decision: Ollie Schmid def. Keiichiro Nakamura by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)

Thomas Petersen vs. Gabriel Lorenco: Lorenco scored a handful of knockdowns in round one to earn a 10-8, on my scorecard. He gassed himself out, though. Petersen then almost finished him at the start of the second round. He gassed himself out doing that, though. In the third both men started very slow, but it was Petersen who showed more grit and summoned up the strength to get Lorenco down and pound him out (and save himself from a likely draw).

Official decision: Thomas Petersen def. Gabriel Lorenco by TKO (ground and pound), round 3 (4:47)

Karine Silva vs. Gabriella Fernandes : This was a highly skippable fight with the first round spent entirely on the fence with neither woman doing anything to advance the position or offer any kind of threat. It picked up a little as the fight wore on, but still looked mostly like sparring. Silva is the busier fighter, so she edged it on my scorecard.

Official decision: Karine Silva def. Gabriella Fernandes by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)

Murtazali Magomedov vs. Jose Delano: These two put on a very close and technical fight. Delano got the first round, for me, with his volume striking. Magomedov got the second round, with his wrestling and a nice head kick. The third was a toss up, with Delano having more gas in the tank and doing more with his striking. But Magomedov scored a knockdown in the final seconds. That gave him the round, and fight, on my scorecard. If not for the knockdown, I would have given that final round to Delano.

Official decision: Murtazali Magomedov def. Jose Delano by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)

Austin Bashi vs. Carlos Calderon: Bashi made quick work of the short notice opponent. He threw some chaotic strikes Calderon's way, but looked much more composed when he got his takedown. On the ground he took the back easily and pounced on a tight rear naked choke/neck crank for the win.

Official decision: Austin Bashi def. Carlos Calderon by submission (rear naked choke), round 1 (1:07)

Andre Petroski vs. Mantas Kondratavicius: Kondratavicius had Petroski in some trouble early on, cracking him with very hard shots every time Petroski thought about a takedown. In the second round, though, Petroski imposed his wrestling game on the former kickboxer. Kondratavicius got trapped underneath and Petroski was able to break him down with ground and pound and snap his three fight losing streak.

Official decision: Andre Petroski def. Mantas Kondratavicius by TKO (ground and pound), round 2 (4:39)

Seokhyeon Ko vs. Wellington Turman: That was all Ko. He was sparking Turman with solid single shots throughout the fight and also got him down with some flashy takedowns. In the second Turman showed he's got some bite on the feet and that led Ko to lean on his wrestling to seal the win here down the stretch.

Official decision: Seokhyeon Ko def. Wellington Turman by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)

Jose Souza vs. Jonny Parsons: Parsons was game for as long as this fight was on, but he didn't have many answers for Souza's length. Souza eventually cracked him with an uppercut and wrapped this up in the second round.

Official decision: Jose Souza def. Jonny Parsons by KO (uppercut), round 2 (4:16)
